claims.claim: The DOJ's September 2024 debit monopolisation complaint against Visa describes the debit pricing structures Mastercard competes against: volume commitments priced so that disloyalty penalties apply to all Visa transactions unless nearly all debit volume runs on Visa, plus payments to would-be competitors; Visa is said to charge roughly USD 8 billion a year in U.S. debit network fees.

claims.publisher: U.S. Department of Justice, Office of Public Affairs
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: Archived press release (updated February 6, 2025); read in the browser pane after WebFetch and curl returned empty bodies. The press release does not mention Mastercard; the complaint text itself was not read (see not_found).

claims.claim: In March 2024 Mastercard announced a class settlement to reduce and cap its U.S. consumer and commercial credit interchange for at least five years and simplify surcharging rules; the court later denied approval and a revised agreement reached in November 2025 is pending.
claims.quote: has reached an agreement to reduce its U.S. credit card interchange rates for at least a five-year period
claims.title: Mastercard commits to lowering U.S. interchange for small businesses and broader merchant community
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: Also verbatim: 'The interchange reduction will effectively serve as a cap for a period of five years and will apply to all U.S.-issued credit programs'. Superseded: the FY2025 10-K states the 2024 Rules Relief settlement 'was subsequently denied by the court' and a revised November 2025 agreement awaits preliminary approval. Newsroom listing showed no Mastercard release on the November 2025 revision. Akamai returns HTTP 403 to WebFetch and curl for mastercard.com/mastercard.us; page read in the browser pane.

claims.claim: Mastercard Developers' Terms of Use describe paid API subscriptions billed monthly, quarterly or yearly at the rate selected when purchasing, with the option of custom plans and prorated refunds on cancellation; no public price list per API was found.
claims.quote: You will be billed at the rate you select and that rate will not change while you are enrolled in that particular plan.
claims.title: Mastercard Developers Terms of Use (Last updated: August 2026)
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: 'Subscriptions' section. Also verbatim: 'All cancellations will trigger a prorated refund, except for custom subscription plans.' and 'You will also have the option to create custom plans that may be handled outside of our standard subscription processing model.' The Quick Start Guide (https://developer.mastercard.com/platform/documentation/quick-start-guide/) describes free self-service Sandbox projects and a 'Request Production access' flow with company verification but states no prices; keys are 'valid for 13 months'. Client SDKs on github.com/Mastercard are open source (Apache-2.0 and MIT licences shown). Page is JavaScript-rendered; read in the browser pane.

claims.claim: The court-authorised MDL 1720 settlement site confirms the Rule 23(b)(3) damages class (merchants accepting Visa or Mastercard January 1, 2004 to January 25, 2019), final approval December 16, 2019, Second Circuit affirmance March 15, 2023, and a second partial distribution approved June 15, 2026 with payments from September 2026.
claims.quote: The lawsuit is about claims that merchants paid excessive fees to accept Visa and Mastercard cards
claims.title: Payment Card Settlement | Official Court-Authorized Website - Home
claims.publisher: Epiq (court-authorised settlement administrator), In re Payment Card Interchange Fee and Merchant Discount Antitrust Litigation, E.D.N.Y. MDL 1720
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: Also: 'On June 15, 2026, the Court approved the motion.' and 'Payments will be issued on a rolling basis in September 2026'. Cloudflare blocks curl (HTTP 403); read in the browser pane. The site names a login-only 'Merchant Portal'.

contradictions.a: Mastercard's March 26, 2024 press release says the Rules Relief class settlement would reduce and cap U.S. credit interchange for five years with rule changes 'most likely in late 2024 or early 2025'.
contradictions.b: Mastercard's FY2025 10-K (Note 19) says that 2024 settlement 'was subsequently denied by the court' and that a revised November 2025 agreement awaits preliminary approval.

contradictions.a: The Federal Reserve Reg II data-collections page presents the calendar-year 2023 report as the latest interchange fee data release.
contradictions.b: The Board's 'Average Debit Card Interchange Fee by Payment Card Network' page shows 2024 per-network figures (e.g. Mastercard covered $0.24 / 0.49%).
